To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the top-antitop production rate at the Tevatron is significantly higher than the current experimental value, (2) the top quark pole mass is 172.5 ± 1.2 GeV, and (3) the top-anti-top cross section in e + e - collisions at √ s = 350 GeV is 1.2 ± 0.2 pb.
the top quark is heavy ( m t = 172.9 ± 0.7 GeV) and that the top-antitop cross section near threshold is significantly larger than previously estimated.
the top quark production rate at the peak is enhanced by 20% with respect to the NLO result, and that the peak is shifted to a slightly higher energy by 0.5 GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the top quark production cross section and mass at the threshold, which will be relevant at the International Linear Collider.
the top quark production near the threshold in e +e − collisions.
the top quark production cross section near threshold in electron-positron collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the top quark is not a pole mass, but that it has an intrinsic width.
the top quark pole mass is not a good mass definition for the top quark.

top quark threshold data will allow for an accurate determination of the top quark pole mass only if one uses an appropriate mass definition and if one has a reliable theoretical control of the cross section at NNLO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NNLO correction to σ ( e + e − → t t → l ν b b ¯ ) is large and positive, and that the top quark is not very heavy.
top quark mass measurements in e + e− collisions are possible, but the accuracy is limited.

a determination of the top mass with an uncertainty of about 100 MeV is possible at the LHC, but a determination at the level of 50 MeV or less requires an e + e − machine with a centre-of-mass energy of 500 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the top quark production rate is sensitive to the details of the short distance dynamics, and that the conventional pole mass definition is not a suitable mass parameter for the top quark.
top quarks produced in e + e collisions near threshold are a promising probe of the dynamics of heavy quarkonium.
the NNLO corrections to the cross section are large and that they are sensitive to the renormalization scheme for the top quark.
